item.title: Riverfront Music Returns! Allianz Amphitheater 2026 Lineup Drops
item.description: Allianz Amphitheater has announced its 2026 concert lineup in Richmond, featuring Alabama Shakes, Sting, The Black Keys, Chris Stapleton, and more. The riverfront venue’s second full season runs from April through September, bringing a wide range of national touring acts to Brown’s Island and downtown Richmond.

item.title: Salon de Résistance | The Iran War
item.description: Salon de Résistance returns March 26 at Black Iris with a live discussion on the escalating war in Iran. Featuring national security experts Joyce Connery, Thomas Countryman, and Dr. Dana El Kurd, the event explores the conflict’s global impact, U.S. involvement, and what comes next.

item.title: Richmond’s Sci-Fi and Fantasy Season Has Arrived. Here’s Where to Go.
item.description: From GalaxyCon to RavenCon, Richmond’s spring lineup of sci-fi, fantasy, and cosplay events brings conventions, immersive theater, and renaissance fairs across the city. Here’s a guide to the biggest fandom gatherings happening in Richmond, Virginia, and what to expect from each.

item.title: New Exhibit ‘We The People’ Explores What It Means to Be a Virginian
item.description: A preview of We The People, a new exhibition at the Virginia Museum of History & Culture exploring immigration in Virginia through personal stories. Featuring insights from curator Julie Kemper and researcher Noah Tinsley, the exhibit looks at identity, history, and what it means to be American today.

item.title: Hemp Retailers Say New Virginia Cannabis Law Would Shut Them Down
item.description: Virginia hemp businesses are urging Governor Spanberger to amend a new cannabis bill that imposes a 2mg THC cap, warning it could eliminate most products and force closures. More than 1,500 small businesses and farmers say the legislation threatens Virginia’s $562 million hemp industry.

item.title: Babe Improv Might Be The Funniest Thing in Richmond Right Now
item.description: Babe Improv is helping define Richmond’s growing comedy scene with unpredictable, fully improvised shows built from audience suggestions. Performers Elizabeth Byland and Anthony Brazeau bring a mix of chaos, trust, and sharp instincts to the stage, creating one-night-only performances that highlight the city’s evolving, accessible, and collaborative comedy community.

item.title: RVA Live Music This Weekend | Gogol Bordello, Slaat, Hagstone, TV Buddha + New Bucko Single
item.description: Richmond’s live music scene heats up this week with Gogol Bordello at The National, stacked hardcore bills at Banditos, and Fuzzy Cactus standouts. Plus, Bucko drops their latest single “The Needle.” A full rundown of must-see shows and rising local acts across RVA’s stages.

item.title: Meet Me @ The Altar Talk Independence, Growth, and ‘Worried Sick’ in Richmond
item.description: Meet Me @ The Altar sit down with RVA Magazine in Richmond to discuss their ‘Worried Sick’ EP, going independent, mental health, and their evolving sound. The pop-punk duo reflects on lessons learned, representation in the scene, and reconnecting with their roots on a new tour.

item.title: Richmond Earns “City of Darkness” Award Over FOIA Concerns
item.description: Richmond has been named a 2026 “City of Darkness” by national watchdogs, citing concerns over its FOIA library and handling of public records. The designation highlights ongoing legal battles, rising taxpayer costs, and broader questions about transparency and accountability in city government as scrutiny continues to grow.

item.title: No Red Carpet, Just Films! James River Film Festival Is Back
item.description: The James River Film Festival returns to Richmond March 29 through April 4, featuring screenings at VMFA, VCU, Studio Two Three, and the Richmond Public Library. The lineup includes Killer of Sheep, Méliès shorts, experimental film, and local filmmakers, along with free online screenings and special guest appearances.
